key_insight: This paper proposes a single framework that links neural superposition to sparse, interpretable latent codes. In simple terms, it shows how hidden features in neural networks can be identified, separated, and evaluated in a consistent way.
problem_solved: Neural networks often mix multiple latent features into shared representations, making them hard to interpret. This work addresses the challenge of disentangling those features and judging whether the resulting codes are truly meaningful and sparse.
method: Introduces a three-step pipeline for identifying latent features in superposed neural representations.
Provides a framework to disentangle overlapping features into sparse, interpretable codes.
Includes a way to assess the quality and interpretability of the recovered latent representations.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this makes it easier to understand what a model has learned and why it makes certain predictions. It can support debugging, interpretability, and more trustworthy model design.
visual_elements: Three-stage flow diagram: identify → disentangle → assess
Side-by-side illustration of superposed vs. sparse interpretable representations
Latent-space scatter plot showing feature overlap and separation
Icon set for interpretability, sparsity, and evaluation
paper_title: A unifying framework from neural superposition to sparse interpretable codes
paper_authors: David Klindt, Charles O’Neill, Patrik Reizinger, Harald Maurer, Nina Miolane
